supporting_evidence: Six championships and six Finals MVPs in six Finals appearances.
counterargument: Finals record ignores losses before the Finals and treats team outcomes as individual outcomes.
analysis_required: Compare complete playoff paths, opponent quality, pre-series expectations, and individual performance.
verdict: Descriptive but not decisive. GOAT Lab evaluates complete playoff paths and expected series outcomes rather than Finals record alone.

supporting_evidence: More Finals appearances across different teams and conferences.
counterargument: Conference strength and Finals losses still need context.
analysis_required: Model path difficulty and expected series probabilities across every round.
verdict: Supports LeBron's longevity and sustained contention, but it does not settle the comparison without path-strength context.

supporting_evidence: Scoring titles, MVP-level seasons, elite defense, and championship peaks.
counterargument: Peak depends on window length and how elite-tail scores are transformed.
analysis_required: Compare best one-, three-, five-, and seven-year era-adjusted windows under multiple scales.
verdict: Not supported by the published default peak category, which favors LeBron. The conclusion remains sensitive to the exact peak definition and scoring scale.

supporting_evidence: More seasons, minutes, and elite late-career production.
counterargument: Longevity should not automatically outweigh a higher peak.
analysis_required: Calculate cumulative value above average and higher historical thresholds.
verdict: Supported by the frozen longevity category. Whether that should outweigh other categories is a user value choice.

supporting_evidence: Higher scoring volume and scoring-title dominance relative to his era.
counterargument: Efficiency, spacing, passing burden, and postseason opponent context also matter.
analysis_required: Compare points per 75, relative efficiency, scoring load, playoff changes, and shot profile.
verdict: Partially tested. v1 does not publish a standalone pure-scoring winner; the final offense category combines scoring and playmaking.

argument: LeBron was the better offensive engine
supporting_evidence: Elite scoring combined with unusually high playmaking responsibility.
counterargument: Ball dominance can affect portability and teammate roles.
analysis_required: Estimate scoring plus creation value, turnover cost, and team offense with and without the player.
verdict: Supported by the published offense category, which favors LeBron, while portability and off-ball fit remain less completely measured.

supporting_evidence: DPOY, defensive teams, steals, point-of-attack reputation, and awards evidence.
counterargument: LeBron offered more positional and help-defense versatility at his best.
analysis_required: Combine awards, box evidence, assignments, and structured film coding.
verdict: Supported by the published defense category, which strongly favors Jordan. Full-career film coverage remains a limitation.

supporting_evidence: More positional size, rebounding, passing roles, and lineup functions.
counterargument: Versatility is not identical to total impact or superiority in a primary role.
analysis_required: Define role dimensions and compare elite-threshold breadth with matched film and lineup evidence.
verdict: Not fully tested in v1. The dashboard shows statistical skill families but does not claim a complete role-versatility verdict.

argument: Jordan had a stronger killer instinct
supporting_evidence: Narratives emphasize late-game aggression and competitive reputation.
counterargument: The phrase is vague, selectively remembered, and difficult to measure.
analysis_required: Operationalize elimination, close-game, comeback, and high-leverage performance with declared samples.
verdict: Not tested rigorously in v1 because 'killer instinct' was not converted into a defensible standalone metric.

supporting_evidence: Selected missed shots and Finals moments are often cited.
counterargument: Career clutch samples and elimination-game performance contradict a simple narrative.
analysis_required: Analyze every declared high-leverage possession and report uncertainty and selection rules.
verdict: Not established by v1. The project does not support a broad anti-clutch conclusion from selected moments.

supporting_evidence: Played with multiple All-Star and All-NBA teammates.
counterargument: Jordan also played on deep championship rosters; named-star counts ignore fit, depth, and health.
analysis_required: Build teammate value excluding the focal player, availability, and expected-title models.
verdict: Not resolved in the central model. Supporting-cast and injury analyses remained diagnostic and added zero extra central weight.

argument: Jordan had the better championship teams
supporting_evidence: Several Bulls teams had elite defenses, continuity, and strong supporting casts.
counterargument: LeBron also played on star-heavy teams and influenced roster construction.
analysis_required: Compare supporting-cast value, coaching continuity, roster health, and preseason expectation.
verdict: Not resolved completely in v1. Team context is shown, but the project does not declare one player's championship rosters universally stronger.

supporting_evidence: Awards, scoring titles, and separation from contemporaries.
counterargument: League talent, expansion, roles, and scaling choices differ across eras.
analysis_required: Use within-season standardization, percentiles, vote shares, and gaps from peers.
verdict: Mixed and scaling-sensitive. The approved career-scoring methods split the overall winner 2-2, showing that era dominance depends on how elite separation is represented.

supporting_evidence: Won with different franchises, coaches, teammates, and tactical roles.
counterargument: Changing teams can also create roster-control advantages.
analysis_required: Measure impact stability across lineup archetypes, teams, coaches, and career stages.
verdict: Descriptively true, but not an independent scored category in v1. It supports the discussion without deciding the full result.

supporting_evidence: Documented global popularity, Jordan Brand influence, and 1990s NBA visibility.
counterargument: Globalization also reflected league strategy, media expansion, the Dream Team, and other players.
analysis_required: Build a sourced timeline and avoid single-cause claims.
verdict: Evidence supports major global influence, but v1 does not claim Jordan alone caused basketball's globalization.

supporting_evidence: Free-agency choices, media ownership, and athlete-business activity influenced later stars.
counterargument: Labor rules and broader athlete trends also contributed.
analysis_required: Analyze direct player statements, transaction patterns, and business milestones.
verdict: Evidence supports meaningful influence, but a single-person causal claim would be too strong.

argument: Jordan's retirement gaps should count against longevity
supporting_evidence: Voluntary missed seasons reduced achieved career value.
counterargument: Some definitions value only played seasons and avoid separate calendar-span penalties.
analysis_required: Publish achieved-career-value and calendar-span views separately.
verdict: They count in the achieved-value framework because missed seasons add no value. v1 does not add a second subjective retirement penalty.

argument: LeBron's 2011 Finals should heavily damage his case
supporting_evidence: Performance declined materially relative to his standard in a favored Finals.
counterargument: One series should be weighted within an entire career, and later performance also matters.
analysis_required: Measure series underperformance versus regular-season level and model expectation.
verdict: The series is included in playoff evidence, but v1 applies no special manual punishment beyond its measured performance and context.

argument: Jordan never lost after reaching the top
supporting_evidence: The Bulls completed two three-peats once championship level was reached.
counterargument: The framing excludes earlier and later playoff losses and retirement decisions.
analysis_required: Use the complete career timeline and avoid conditional cherry-picking.
verdict: Selective framing rather than a standalone analytical measure. v1 evaluates complete careers and full playoff paths.

argument: LeBron's all-time totals make him the GOAT
supporting_evidence: Record cumulative scoring and broad career totals reflect rare sustained value.
counterargument: Totals mix ability, durability, era, pace, and number of seasons.
analysis_required: Separate totals, per-possession rates, peak, and cumulative value above thresholds.
verdict: Strongly supports LeBron's longevity case, but totals alone do not decide the full nine-category model.
